title: Canonical TanStack endpoint caches and client-mutation invalidation

acceptanceCriteria.description: Shared frontend GET endpoints use the canonical endpointQueryKeys owner, the hand-rolled cachedReads/cachedSafe layer and Packages module cache are removed, and no migrated endpoint retains a competing legacy key.

Client create, update, delete, active-toggle, and store-sync mutation paths delegate to one client-cache invalidation owner covering the canonical client, store, count, and inventory families; the obsolete ['inventory'] alias is rejected.

The Orders and Dashboard client-count scenario shares one TanStack cache entry, one root invalidation produces one refetch, and the real Clients-page mutation callbacks are statically bound to that canonical invalidator rather than a synthetic-only path.
The focused PS-458, PS-448, cache-hygiene, failure-state, and Settings guards pass together with strict TypeScript, the production Vite build, and all 56 mandatory source-of-truth commands.

Backend endpoints remain authoritative for every DTO and business value; the frontend helper owns only request invalidation identity and changes no money, rates, labels, inventory quantity, billing, auth/scope, provider routing, or shipped/cancelled protection.

The closure is exact-SHA governed, adds no migration, rejects stale or malformed proof, and records the earlier audit blocker plus its bounded correction without claiming any live customer or provider mutation.

canonicalOwners: backend API endpoints own every returned DTO and business value
web/src/lib/endpoint-query-keys.ts owns canonical frontend request identities
web/src/lib/client-query.ts owns the canonical client-list keys and query options
web/src/lib/client-cache-invalidation.ts#invalidateClientDependentQueries owns the frontend cache families invalidated by successful client mutations
web/src/lib/query-client.ts owns the singleton TanStack Query client used for dedupe, freshness, retention, and refetch

oldOwners.path: web/src/pages/Clients_variants/useClientsData.tsx and InventoryView.tsx per-view client invalidation lists

wrappers.delegatesTo: backend endpoints for data and the canonical frontend invalidator after successful client mutations
backend client routes for mutations and the shared invalidator for cache freshness

sotBypass.details: The new helper never computes or chooses business values. It only enumerates TanStack Query families that must be marked stale after backend-owned mutations, removing two competing invalidation lists.

evidence.proves: Orders and Dashboard share one client query, a successful mutation invalidates one root and refetches once, and the real API/Clients-page mutation boundaries delegate to the same client/store/count/inventory invalidation owner.
The audit blocker is corrected at the actual mutation entry points, every named canonical family is present, and the duplicate Inventory-view invalidation list is removed.

evidence.proves: The legacy read-cache layer and migrated view-specific key aliases remain absent while Dashboard, Billing, Inventory, Packages, Locations, and Settings use the TanStack owner.

evidence.command: npm run test:frontend-failure-states && npm run test:settings-query-migration
evidence.proves: Transport errors still fail visibly, destructive client callers handle rejections, and Settings query migration behavior stays intact.

evidence.proves: The documentation names backend DTO authority, the frontend request-identity owner, the earliest stale-data injection point, delegating callers, and the mutation-consistency boundary.

evidence.command: npm run typecheck && npm run build:web with inert Vite environment values
evidence.proves: Strict backend/frontend TypeScript passes and the production Vite build completes with 2,979 modules transformed.

evidence.command: npm run test:sot-guard-pack with inert localhost/.invalid environment values and a dummy test-only JWT secret
evidence.proves: All 56 mandatory source-of-truth, rate, label, billing, inventory, auth/scope, lifecycle, migration-readiness, worker, and governance commands pass offline.
Complete packets pass and malformed or unsupported evidence is rejected deterministically.
Wrong branch/SHA, stale proof, source-of-truth bypass, and unmet critical criteria cannot produce a green closure.
Injected malformed, stale, incomplete, and false-green packets are rejected or score-capped.

migrations.rollbackPlan: No schema rollback is needed. If PS-458 must be reversed, use reviewed forward reverts of the bounded mutation-invalidation correction and the original cache-unification commit; do not alter migration history or production data.

rollback.strategy: Forward-revert the PS-458 correction and packet commits. A product rollback may separately forward-revert the original cache-unification implementation while preserving all backend DTO, database, migration, and historical order/shipment facts.

liveVerification.reason: Acceptance is frontend cache-identity and mutation-wiring behavior that is fully exercised by in-memory/static guards and a production build. Mutating a real production client solely for certification would create avoidable customer-scope impact; deployment health and exact-SHA parity are verified separately after push.
